found_by: code review (altitude): ext4_dir_find_in_block bounded its walk by the searched name length, not by the entry header
base: mke2fs -b 1024 -O ^dir_index,^metadata_csum,^64bit -I 128 on 2 MiB, a directory /d with three files

edits.what: the last real entry in /d's block, rec_len shrunk to its true length
edits.note: so the walk continues into the crafted tail

edits.what: a filler entry (inode 0) advancing the cursor to offset 1023
edits.note: one byte before the 1024-byte block end
so ext4_dir_en_get_inode reads nonzero and the old code dereferences the header

symptom: Looking up a 1-byte name walked to a directory entry one byte short of the block end; the old guard `de + name_len > addr_limit` used the SEARCHED name's length, so the entry passed it and ext4_dir_find_in_block then read the inode, name_len, name and rec_len past the block buffer: AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at ext4_dir.c:718, reached from ext4_dir_find_entry on an ordinary lookup.
fixed_by: patch 0071/0072 -- the walk bounds the fixed 8-byte header, then the entry's own name_len, before either is read
reproduce: build/bin/ext4dump cat /d/z # ASan clean with the patch, heap-buffer-overflow without it
note_on_detection: A read overflow, so it faults only under AddressSanitizer -- the hostile suite catches it when run against the debug/ASan tools (make test-asan), exactly as fixtures 0001 and 0004 do. Under an optimised build the stray read is silent.
